title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'suite' of La Longue Marche, numbered pages around 687. The page is a group-scheme computation over a base S_0 = Spec Z_{ρ0}, with bad behaviour above the prime 3. The likely background is the Galois action on the torsion of the (profinite) modular group, i.e. the stabilisers of order 4 and 6 in SL2(Z). The identification is my inference from L_ρ ≃ (Z/4Z), a group O_12^* (probably the group scheme of units of Z/12Z) and a character ε_3 with values ±1; it is not stated on the page.

Notation, as I read it:
- G^+ is an extension of a finite group by a 'linear' part M (G^+ ⊃ M, H^+ = G^+/M).
- ρ is a section of order 4.
- N_ρ is its normaliser, Z_ρ its centraliser, L_ρ ≃ Z/4 the cyclic group it generates.
- χ_ρ : N_ρ → O_12^* records the exponent action, through a 'cyclotomic-like' character whose 3-component is ε_3.

First step (previous page and top of this one). The naive normaliser has a centraliser part Z^0_ρ = Z_ρ ∩ M = Ker(1−ρ_M) on M. This part is zero off the prime 3 but jumps to dimension 1 in the fibre at 3. Grothendieck therefore replaces N_ρ by the schematic closure of its restriction over S_0 − {3}. This gives a 'better' flat group scheme, still written N_ρ, which fits in the exact sequence (159): 1 → L_ρ → N_ρ → O_12^* → 1.

Main step on this page.
- Set G♮_{ρ,σ} = O_12^* · S♮, with S♮ = M, a subgroup of G_{ρ,σ} = O_12^* · S^+.
- Set N♮_ρ = N_ρ ∩ G♮.
- Since N♮ ∩ L_ρ = M ∩ L_ρ = 1, N♮ injects into O_12^* via χ_ρ.

Claim (162): the image is O'^*_12 = {μ | ε_3(μ) = 1} (equivalently v_3(μ) = 0). A marginal remark adds that N♮ ⊂ Z_ρ, so it should be called Z♮_ρ.
- Containment of O'^*_12 in the image is said to follow from (159).
- For the reverse inclusion, take a local section u = f^{-1}u_μ with f ∈ ΓM and μ ∈ ΓO_12^*. The normaliser condition gives λ^ν ρ = int(f) ρ^{ε_3} (completed on the next page). Reducing mod M gives ρ = ρ^{ε_3}, so ε_3 = 1.

Consequence: Z♮_ρ is a partial section, over the index-2 subgroup O'^*_12, of the extension N_ρ of O_12^* by L_ρ. The next page asks whether an extra element τ' = τσ normalises it, in order to obtain a full splitting of (159) or to control it. This is a technical lemma in the construction of schematic models over Z of the normalisers of torsion elements.
errors: Equation numbers are reused: (159) is used on the previous page for the equation (1−ρ_M)x = 0 and again here for the exact sequence; (161) is used twice.
'N_ρ défini dans (157)' should probably refer to (155), where N_ρ is introduced via the exact sequence; (157) is the map Z_ρ → L_ρ.

The claim that O'^*_12 is contained in the image 'résulte de (159)' is not justified. Surjectivity of χ_ρ in (159) does not by itself give lifts lying inside G♮ = O_12^*·M. One needs that the lifts of μ with ε_3(μ) = 1 can be chosen in G♮ (presumably u_μ itself, or u_μ corrected by an element of M, centralises ρ when ε_3 = 1). This is a small gap; it is plausibly filled by the definition of u_μ in (151).

ideas.what: Replace a non-flat centraliser/normaliser group scheme, which jumps in dimension at the bad prime 3, by the schematic closure of its restriction to the good locus S_0 − {3}.
ideas.modern_name: Flat closure (schematic closure) of a group scheme; Néron-type 'good model' of a stabiliser
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (EGA IV, SGA 3; Bruhat–Tits style flat closures)

ideas.what: Exact sequence 1 → L_ρ → N_ρ → O_12^* → 1, normaliser of a torsion element modulo its centraliser, with the quotient identified with a group of 'exponent' units modulo 12.
ideas.modern_name: Normaliser/centraliser of finite-order elements (torsion of SL2(Z) and of the profinite modular groups) with cyclotomic-character action
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller setting, work on the GT action on torsion and inertia (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) discusses the torsion of Teichmüller groups and the 'quasi-torsion'; the precise schematic version here is unsure

ideas.what: The intersection with the 'linear' part G♮ = O_12^*·M is a partial section of the extension over the index-2 subgroup ker ε_3; proof by reduction mod M.
ideas.modern_name: Partial splitting of a group extension; computing the image of a centraliser

missed.claim: Grothendieck builds schematic (over Spec Z localised) models of the normalisers of torsion elements, with special care at the primes 2 and 3. This suggests arithmetic group-scheme models of the Teichmüller/modular group data that encode the bad primes of M_{1,1}. As far as I know no published development takes this group-scheme-over-Z viewpoint for these normalisers. However, the page is a routine technical step and its identification with this program is my inference.
missed.quote: On trouve dans un groupe meilleur, que je noterai encore N_ρ, s'inscrivant dans la suite exacte (159) 1 → L_ρ → N_ρ → O_12^* → 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and schematic models of the automorphism data at the elliptic points j = 0 and j = 1728 (primes 2 and 3) are relevant to stacky models of M_{1,1} over Z and to Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory, though the content of this single page is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical, mostly routine lemma: flat closure plus computing the image of a normaliser intersected with a subgroup. It is part of an unpublished program on schematic models of normalisers of torsion elements over Z. The program as a whole is interesting, but nothing on this page is a striking standalone result.
transcription_corrections: 'par d'ailleurs schématiques de [?] restriction en dessous [?] de S_0 − {3}' should likely read 'par l'adhérence schématique de sa restriction au-dessus de S_0 − {3}'.

'On trouve dans un [?] groupe meilleur, que je noterai [?] par contre [?] N_ρ' should likely read 'On trouve donc un sous-groupe meilleur, que je noterai désormais encore N_ρ, s'inscrivant dans la suite exacte'.
The marginal note should read 'donc N♮_ρ ⊂ Z_ρ, il vaudrait mieux le noter Z♮_ρ'.
In (160) the factor under M is S♮ (written as a 'G♮'-like gothic letter), with the annotation '= ΓM' added above f ∈ ΓS♮.
